label: Opt-in reconstructed 1904 working dress (shirtwaist, dark skirt, white bib apron) on the shared portable rig
basis: Original reusable shirtwaist bodice with a standing collar, gathered dark skirt, front apron with a bib laid over the bodice, and source-fitted closed shoes, cut after the working dress the 1903 Wasson stereographs show (T-3423). Seams, proportions and colours are conjectural. Complete source anatomy remains unchanged beneath clothing. No accepted photographic or historical personal likeness.
source_scope: Three actually viewed 1903 C. L. Wasson studio stereographs (LOC, no known restrictions) supply the silhouette of a working woman's pale shirtwaist and standing collar, a bib apron and a long dark skirt, and the swept-up hair of the decade. They are not Chicago and not of the Glessner household; no image pixels or traced garment shapes enter the asset.
